rationale: Requested execution of the three-order probe, which adds the discriminating delivery order in which the command-carrying reply is adopted last before the quorum trigger. Local feedback on the added order keeps the owner's command while the two orders recorded by the previous receipt lose it, so the receipt for this revision should show the adopted value following the order rather than the reply set.

scope.description: Owner replica 0 proposes X on its own instance (0,0), replica 1's non-equal pre-accept reply is delivered and replica 1 then fails, so the owner enters the Accept phase at ballot 0 towards replicas 2 and 3; replica 3 accepts without ever pre-accepting (its state holds no command), and the owner's AcceptReplies are left in flight. The owner, alive and still holding X, then runs startRecoveryForInstance(0,0); the harness delivers the Prepare replies of replicas 2, 3 and 4 in a chosen order (replica 2 carries X at value ballot 0, replicas 3 and 4 carry no command at the same ballot) and records whether the owner re-proposes a command and what its instance holds afterwards. The test runs the same message set twice with the empty reply last in one run and first in the other. The order parameter is now applied: run A delivers the replies in the order 2,4,3, run B in the order 3,4,2 and run C in the order 3,2,4, and each run records the order actually delivered.
assumptions: Same construction, transport boundary and crash model as the other experiments in this harness.
Delivery order among the prepare replies is chosen by the harness, which is what a real network does not fix; the read order is not altered.
The number of delivered prepare replies (self plus three peers) means the quorum trigger fires at the second peer reply, which is what the two orders are meant to probe.
excluded: No client path, no state-machine execution, no run() loop or recovery timer loop.

experiment.prefix: The harness drives the owner's proposal and accept phase through the target's own handlers, fails replica 1 after its reply, delivers the Accept to replicas 2 and 3, then calls the owner's startRecoveryForInstance(0,0) and delivers each collected PrepareReply to the owner, recording the owner's leader-bookkeeping state (status, appended count, nacks, prepared flag) and the instance's command length before and after the dispatch. Each recipient's messages are collected before delivery and then delivered in the order declared for that run, with the delivered order recorded.
experiment.requirement: A recovery of an instance must not drop the instance's command when a reply without a command arrives at the same value ballot as replies that carry one, and the adopted value must not depend on the delivery order of equally admissible replies.
experiment.responsibility: The recovering replica's own adoption loop and dispatch (epaxos/epaxos.go:1239-1246 and 1291-1313): the replies are the acceptors' honest answers at their stored ballots.

comparisons.description: Run A (replies 2,4,3): the instance still holds the owner's command after the recovery; violated when an empty command is adopted instead.

Run B (replies 3,4,2): with the command-carrying reply arriving last among the delivered set, the instance still holds the owner's command; a violated outcome here shows the adopted value is fixed by the replies present when the quorum trigger fires rather than by the full set.

Run C (replies 3,2,4): the command-carrying reply is the second delivered, so it is the last adopted before the quorum trigger; the instance is expected to keep the owner's command here, which would show the outcome is fixed by which reply is adopted last before the trigger rather than by the reply set.

experiment.revision_reason: Added a third delivery order, 3,2,4, in which the command-carrying reply is the second one delivered and therefore the last adopted before the quorum trigger. This is the discriminating case: the first two orders put an empty reply in that position, while this one puts the command-carrying reply there. Scenario, handlers and compared fields are unchanged.
